dotGuide.intro: Clever, quick, and full of curiosity — a fox is one of nature's most fascinating animals to draw! With its pointed ears, bushy tail, and bright eyes, this 58-dot puzzle builds the fox up section by section. Grab a pencil, find a comfortable spot, and let this little fox leap onto the page!

sections.title: The Pointed Ears and Forehead
sections.learn: Start at dot 1 and work through to dot 14 to draw the fox's sharp, pointed ears and rounded forehead. The triangular ear shapes reward careful, confident strokes — encourage children to pause and look at the next dot before each line.
sections.fact: A fox's ears can rotate independently, letting it pinpoint exactly where a sound is coming from — even a mouse rustling under 30 cm of snow.

sections.title: The Face and Sly Snout
sections.learn: Continue from dot 15 to dot 30 to draw the fox's slender face and pointed snout. This section has shorter, closer-together lines that reward a slow, precise hand — great practice for pencil control.
sections.fact: Foxes have vertically slit pupils, similar to cats, which help them see clearly in both bright daylight and low light. Their eyesight is sharp enough to spot a rabbit from over 100 metres away.

sections.title: The Body
sections.learn: Trace dots 31 through 44 to draw the fox's lithe, agile body. The strokes here are longer and smoother — a satisfying change of rhythm after the detailed face section.
sections.fact: Foxes are solitary hunters but live in family groups called 'leashes' or 'earths'. They cache surplus food by burying it, and have been observed using landmarks to find their hidden stashes later.

sections.title: The Legs and Paws
sections.learn: Connect dots 45 to 54 to add the fox's nimble legs and delicate paws. The paw shapes are small and rounded — remind children to take their time here for the neatest result.
sections.fact: Foxes walk on their toes, not their heels, which gives them a light, quiet step — perfect for sneaking up on prey. In winter, their paws grow extra fur between the pads for grip on icy ground.

sections.title: The Bushy Tail
sections.learn: Finish by connecting dots 55 through 58 to complete the fox's magnificent bushy tail. Just four dots to go — a smooth, sweeping finish brings the whole fox to life. Don't forget to colour it!
sections.fact: A fox's tail — called a 'brush' — can be up to 70% of its body length. Foxes use their tail like a blanket in winter, wrapping it around their nose and paws to stay warm while they sleep.

dotGuide.outro: Fantastic work finishing 58 dots! Your fox is ready for a forest background and some autumn colours. Why not draw some leaves or a tree beside your new friend? Discover more free dot to dot printables for every age.

colorSchemes.name: Classic Red Fox
colorSchemes.note: The red fox is the most widespread wild carnivore in the world, instantly recognisable by its russet coat and white-tipped tail.

mapping.why: Red fox ears are vivid russet-orange on the outside, which stands out against the darker forehead fur.
Most red foxes have pale cream or white fur on their cheeks and around the muzzle, contrasting with the orange body.
The fox's back and sides are a deep, rich orange-red — the colour most people picture when they think of a fox.
Red foxes have distinctive dark brown or black legs and paws, like they are wearing dark socks.

mapping.color: Crayola Burnt Orange with white tip
mapping.why: The fox's tail is mostly orange with a bright white tip — colour the last section white to get this right.
